failedChecks: Spec conformance: the owner-approved case 3 is 'search completed cleanly with zero matches, but the youngest unresolved marker is YOUNGER THAN the 30s floor'. The diff also routes a marker with a MISSING timestamp to exit 20 - observed directly in the changed test 'pre-mutation duplicate gate blocks a marker with a missing timestamp', whose assertion moved from EXIT.STATE_ERROR to EXIT.INDEX_LAG_BLOCKED. An unmeasurable marker age is not 'younger than the floor'; this is a user-visible contract change outside the approved scope, and the test edit enshrines it silently.

Doc accuracy (JIRA_QUEUE.md): the new sentence says exit 20 means blocked 'because a completed zero-match search occurred before the youngest unresolved marker reached the Jira search-index-lag age floor'. Per the finding above, exit 20 is also returned for a marker with no parseable timestamp, which that sentence does not describe.

Doc completeness (CLI help text): the requirement was that BOTH JIRA_QUEUE.md and the built-in help note which prior 'unavailable' cases still map to exit 2. JIRA_QUEUE.md does ('poll exhaustion and search failure remain exit 2'); the help text does not.

Doc overclaim (CLI help text): 'Exit code 20 means a pre-mutation operation is blocked pending Jira search-index lag' is broader than the implementation. submitDraft's retry-verification path ('submit refused until the retry verification interval has elapsed') is also a pre-mutation wait-for-index-lag condition and still exits 2. Wording should be narrowed to the pre-mutation duplicate gate specifically.

Packet integrity: the review instructions claim preMutationDuplicateGate is 'fully visible within this diff's context lines'. It is not - the hunk starts at line 1126, mid-function, so the guard condition governing the direct/duplicate early-return branch is not shown. Behavior preservation still holds structurally (the ternary's else branch is byte-identical to the prior code and reason === 'index-lag' is true at exactly one changed return site), but the packet's visibility claim is inaccurate and should be corrected rather than relied on.

No evidence supplied that consumers of exit 2 elsewhere in the repo (calling skills, wrapper scripts, CI, SKILL.md exit-code tables) were surveyed. This is declared public-contract work; splitting a code out of 2 silently breaks any consumer that branches on 2 alone. Only 3 files were touched and no grep evidence accompanies the packet.

securityFindings.summary: Exit 20 carries retry-later semantics ('waiting for the search index to catch up'). It is now also returned for markers with an absent timestamp. If youngestMarkerAgeMs treats an absent 'at' as age 0 (unverifiable from the packet), that draft can never satisfy the floor, so an automated caller that treats 20 as transient will retry indefinitely against Jira. Duplicate-prevention itself is NOT weakened - every case that blocked before still blocks; this is exit-code taxonomy, not a hole in the mutation gate.

Splitting a previously-shared exit code without an audit of downstream consumers can silently reclassify a 'blocked, do not proceed' outcome as an unrecognized failure (or, in a poorly written wrapper, fall through a default branch). No consumer survey is included in the packet.

materialDissent: I do not accept the packet's framing that this is purely exit-code selection with no other user-visible change. The missing-timestamp case is a second, unapproved semantic reclassification riding along in the same diff, and it is only detectable by noticing that one pre-existing test's expected exit code changed.

I dissent from any reading that the CLI's exit contract is now coherent. Exit 20 does not cover all 'blocked pending index lag' conditions - submitDraft's retry-verification interval path remains exit 2. I do NOT recommend changing that path in this diff (it is outside the owner's approved scope); the in-scope remedy is narrowing the help-text wording. Whether the retry-verify path should eventually share exit 20 is an owner question, not a required fix here.

Contrary to a plausible objection, I do not treat the new negative test's audit assertions as insufficient. After this change, exit 2 plus a 'verify-inconclusive' audit event uniquely identifies poll exhaustion (index-lag now exits 20), so the test does discriminate the two cases. Asserting the audit 'reason' field would be a nice tightening, not a defect.
unresolvedQuestions: What does youngestMarkerAgeMs return for a marker with no 'at' field, and can such a marker ever satisfy VERIFY_CLEAR_MIN_AGE_FLOOR_MS? If not, the condition is permanent and exit 20's retry semantics are wrong for it.

Does any other file in the repo (calling skills, SKILL.md exit-code tables, wrapper scripts, CI job) branch on exit code 2 for the Jira CLI in a way that now misses the index-lag case? Requires a repo-wide grep the reviewer cannot run under packet-only rules.

In submitDraft, the earlier localDuplicateGate call maps any blocked result to EXIT.DUPLICATE unconditionally and was intentionally left unchanged. Can that call ever reach the index-lag return (i.e. does a non-empty unresolvedDuplicateEntries/unresolvedDirectEvidence always trigger the gate's first early return)? The guard is not visible in the diff; if it can fall through, an index-lag block would surface as exit 6 there.

Can the gate's direct/duplicate early return ever produce keys.length === 0 while blocked? If so it falls to EXIT.STATE_ERROR, which matches prior behavior, but confirm no path was intended to reach exit 20 there.
Does makeState accept a second 'overrides' argument carrying poll config as used by the new negative test? Not shown in the diff; the implementer's green run is the only evidence.
review.recommendation: Revise, then re-review - the core change is correct and genuinely narrow, and one defect blocks a pass. Required fixes: (1) Stop routing markers with an unparseable/absent timestamp to exit 20. Either return reason 'search-unavailable' for unmeasurable marker age, or introduce a separate reason that maps to EXIT.STATE_ERROR, and revert the 'blocks a marker with a missing timestamp' test assertion to EXIT.STATE_ERROR (add an explicit comment that the malformed-marker case is deliberately NOT index-lag). If the owner instead wants malformed markers under exit 20, that is a spec amendment and must be recorded, not implied by a test edit. (2) Narrow the help-text sentence to 'blocked by the pre-mutation duplicate gate pending Jira search-index lag' and add that poll exhaustion and search failure remain exit 2, matching JIRA_QUEUE.md. (3) Update the JIRA_QUEUE.md exit-20 sentence to match whatever (1) settles on. (4) Before merge, grep the repo for consumers of exit 2 from kstack-jira.mjs (skills, wrappers, CI) and confirm none silently lose the case-3 signal. Confirmed good and needing no change: EXIT.INDEX_LAG_BLOCKED = 20 with no collision against 16-19; the inventory self-test updated to include 20 while still asserting 10-12 absent (deepEqual on the sorted values array also catches duplicates); the ternary chain parses as intended and its else branch is byte-identical to prior behavior, so poll exhaustion, search failure, keyed duplicates, and the empty-keys blocked path all exit exactly as before; submit/unfreeze/discard each have exit-20 coverage plus explicit negative coverage for exit 2 with audit-event assertions; exit 20 is correctly listed as dry-run reachable (the submit dry-run test proves it); no duplicate-detection, poll, marker-age-floor, or verification logic changed; and the approved spec file is untouched by this diff. No part of this belongs back in kstack-interrogate - the scope did not grow.
review.strongestObjection: The change quietly reclassifies a case the owner never approved. Case 3 as approved is 'the marker is younger than the 30-second floor' - a transient condition that clears by waiting. The diff also sends markers with a MISSING timestamp to exit 20, visible only because the pre-existing test 'pre-mutation duplicate gate blocks a marker with a missing timestamp' had its expectation flipped from EXIT.STATE_ERROR to EXIT.INDEX_LAG_BLOCKED with no comment or note in the packet. A timestampless marker has no measurable age; if youngestMarkerAgeMs treats it as age 0 it can never satisfy the floor, so the CLI would be telling callers 'wait and retry' about a draft that is permanently stuck and actually needs human repair - the exact opposite of what the new code is supposed to signal, and a regression from the generic exit 2 that correctly meant 'operator intervention required'.
